about: 3D weapon models (#10511). Each weapon's identity is its accepted refreshed paper-doll layer (authoring/gen-raw/worn/texture-234-record-NNN, `icon`); classic first-person frames add construction detail only where firstPerson.use says so (`compared`: checked against them, and nothing taken). Lengths are overall, in metres. subject and invent are the H3 turnaround request (authoring/tools/weapons/h3.py); grip and parts are how build.py builds the model from the icon. secondGrip is where the off hand closes on a weapon held in both hands: a point in the held-look frame (metres; origin at the grip, +Z toward the pommel or butt), measured as hand_l from hand_r along the weapon_r bone in the idle clip of the family that draws it (0.142 FPP_Longs_Idle, 0.508 FPP_Halb_Idle).
style: Keep the reference's painted dark-fantasy look: its own colours, broad painted colour areas and plain fittings, now as one solid three-dimensional object with real thickness, bevels and edges. The set is one kit: steel blades and heads, antique-brass fittings, red-brown leather wrapped grips, oiled brown wood. No photorealism, glossy modern redesign or microtexture; no added gems, runes, engraving, inscriptions, faces, chains, tassels or ornament the reference does not show.
pose: One complete standalone weapon standing upright, point or head at the top and pommel or butt at the bottom, centred with generous margin and frozen in shape. Its broad face is toward the camera at the start. Keep the tip, guard, grip and pommel fully inside the image. No hand, arm, person, scabbard, sheath, stand, hanger or other object. Neutral grey background.
orbit: One uninterrupted smooth 360-degree CAMERA orbit over five seconds around the upright weapon. Begin square FRONT immediately, pass a true SIDE (edge-on) around 1.25 seconds, square BACK around 2.5 seconds, the independently generated opposite SIDE around 3.75 seconds, and return square FRONT before the final frame. The final camera direction and pose match the start. Fixed height and distance, distant long telephoto near-orthographic view, constant scale and even lighting. Only camera azimuth changes. No cuts, zooms, camera push-in, reframing or pose transitions. Both sides are generated independently, never made by mirroring an image. Centre the complete weapon with generous margin; no cropped tip, guard, grip, pommel or butt.

weapons.name: dagger

firstPerson.why: its spiked guard crown was rejected (#10479); the icon's crescent guard replaces it

weapons.subject: A short straight double-edged steel dagger: a leaf-shaped blade tapering to a sharp point with a raised central ridge, a broad antique-brass crossguard whose two arms curve up toward the point in a crescent, a short grip bound in red-brown leather straps, and a round fluted brass pommel.
weapons.invent: The guard is a solid brass bar, thicker at the centre where it meets the blade, its arms rounded in section. The blade is a flattened diamond in section; seen edge-on it is thin with a visible central ridge. The grip is round in section, as long as the visible grip pieces plus the joined middle.

weapons.name: tanto

firstPerson.why: plain blade only

weapons.subject: A short single-edged Japanese knife: a broad straight steel blade with a clipped angular tip, a round brass tsuba guard, a grip wrapped in red-brown leather cord and a small brass end cap.
weapons.invent: The tsuba is a flat round disc at right angles to the blade. The grip is oval in section. The blade is thick at its back and thin at its edge.

weapons.name: staff

firstPerson.why: the iron end caps, which the icon shows too

weapons.subject: A long plain wooden quarterstaff: one straight oiled brown wooden pole of even thickness with a small dark iron cap at each end.
weapons.invent: The pole is round in section and straight, with the same cap at both ends.

weapons.name: shortsword

firstPerson.why: plain blade only

weapons.subject: A short straight double-edged steel sword: a broad blade tapering to a point with a raised central ridge, a brass crossguard whose arms sweep gently toward the point, a grip bound in red-brown leather and a flared brass pommel.
weapons.invent: The guard is a brass bar, thicker at the centre. The blade is a flattened diamond in section. The grip is round in section and continuous from guard to pommel.

weapons.name: wakizashi

firstPerson.why: plain blade only

weapons.subject: A short gently curved Japanese sword: a single-edged steel blade, a round brass tsuba guard with a brass collar, a long grip wrapped in crossed red-brown leather cord, and a brass end cap.
weapons.invent: The tsuba is a flat round disc at right angles to the blade. The blade is thick at its back and thin at its edge. The grip is oval in section.

weapons.name: broadsword

firstPerson.why: plain blade only

weapons.subject: A straight double-edged steel broadsword: a long blade with a central ridge, a thin brass crossguard with a central block and small flared ends, a grip bound in red-brown leather and a small round brass pommel.
weapons.invent: The guard is a narrow bar, rectangular in section. The blade is a flattened diamond in section. The grip is round in section and continuous from guard to pommel.

weapons.name: saber

firstPerson.why: plain blade only

weapons.subject: A curved single-edged steel saber: a slim blade sweeping back to a sharp point, a round brass bell guard around the blade's base, a brass knuckle bow curving down to the pommel, and a dark leather grip.
weapons.invent: The bell is a shallow round brass cup at right angles to the blade, open toward the grip. The knuckle bow is a thin brass strip on the edge side. The grip is oval in section.

weapons.name: longsword

firstPerson.why: plain blade only

weapons.subject: A long straight double-edged steel sword: a long narrow blade with parallel edges tapering only near its sharp point, a slim antique-brass crossguard whose straight arms widen slightly into flat ends, a grip bound in red-brown leather, and a small round brass pommel.
weapons.invent: The crossguard is a narrow brass bar, rectangular in section, with a small central block where it meets the blade. The blade is a flattened diamond in section with a shallow central ridge; seen edge-on it is thin and straight. The grip is round in section and long enough for one hand, joined continuously from guard to pommel.

weapons.name: katana

firstPerson.why: plain blade only

weapons.subject: A slender curved Japanese sword: a long single-edged steel blade, a small round brass tsuba guard, and a long grip wrapped in crossed red-brown leather cord.
weapons.invent: The tsuba is a flat round disc at right angles to the blade. The blade is thick at its back and thin at its edge. The grip is oval in section and long enough for two hands.

weapons.name: claymore

firstPerson.why: plain blade only

weapons.subject: A great two-handed steel sword: a long straight blade with a central ridge and a small pair of side lugs a hand's length above the guard, a wide thin brass crossguard ending in small balls, a long grip bound in red-brown leather and a small round brass pommel.
weapons.invent: The guard is a straight thin bar. The lugs are small flat steel points on the blade's edges. The blade is a flattened diamond in section. The grip is round in section and long enough for two hands.

weapons.name: dai-katana

firstPerson.why: plain blade only

weapons.subject: A very long curved two-handed Japanese sword: a long single-edged steel blade, a small round brass tsuba guard with a brass collar, a long grip wrapped in crossed red-brown leather cord and a brass end cap.
weapons.invent: The tsuba is a flat round disc at right angles to the blade. The blade is thick at its back and thin at its edge. The grip is oval in section and long enough for two hands.

weapons.name: mace
weapons.note: The flanged head of the classic first-person frames; its paper-doll art is new (authoring/gen-raw/worn/texture-mace-record-*, #10581).

firstPerson.why: the flanges seen from the side and below

weapons.subject: A one-handed flanged mace: a short steel head of five or six broad flat flanges running along its length, parallel to the haft, each a plate with a straight outer edge, around a central steel core, with a short steel spike at the tip and a ringed steel collar below; a straight oiled brown wooden haft, the lower part bound in red-brown leather straps for the grip, ending in a steel butt cap.
weapons.invent: The flanges are spaced evenly round the head and are the same on every side; seen end-on the head is a star of flat plates around a round core. The haft is round in section. The grip binding is continuous from where the wood ends to the butt cap.

weapons.name: club
weapons.note: A new weapon type (#10581): the spiked ball of the mace's classic paper-doll art. Item 124 keeps the name mace and takes the flanged head.

firstPerson.why: the flanged head is the mace's (#10581)

weapons.subject: A one-handed spiked club: a round iron ball head studded all over with short conical spikes, set in a short iron collar on top of a straight oiled brown wooden haft; the lower haft is bound in red-brown leather straps for the grip and ends in a flat iron butt cap.
weapons.invent: The ball is a sphere with about a dozen evenly spaced short spikes, the same on every side. The haft is round in section. The leather grip binding is continuous from where the wood ends to the butt cap.

weapons.name: flail

firstPerson.why: the same ball and links, and the conical socket with its ring at the haft's top; the haft is shorter so the ball can hang in view

weapons.subject: A flail: a straight oiled wooden handle with a steel cap and ring at its end, a chain of oval iron links hanging from the ring, and a round iron ball studded all over with short conical spikes at the end of the chain.
weapons.invent: The handle is round in section. The chain links are oval rings, each turned at right angles to the next. The ball has the same spikes on every side.

weapons.name: warhammer

firstPerson.why: the head follows a real war hammer instead, at Patch's direction (#10574)

weapons.subject: A two-handed war hammer after a real one (Patch's reference): a long oiled wooden haft with riveted steel langets down its flanks, and a steel head set across its top: a compact socket block, a waisted neck with a collar flaring to a square hammer face on the striking side, and a curved spike on the other.
weapons.invent: The classic's block matches no real war hammer, so the head departs from the icon and the classic frames at Patch's direction. The face stays larger than the reference's, to read at game distance. The haft is round in section.

weapons.name: battle-axe

firstPerson.why: the head comes from the icon; Patch kept the plain socket over the classic rounded socket and rings (#10575)

weapons.subject: A one-handed battle axe: a straight oiled wooden haft with a leather-bound grip, and a single broad bearded steel blade with a curved cutting edge, fixed to a steel socket at the top of the haft.
weapons.invent: The blade is flat and thin at its edge, thickening toward the socket. The socket is a short steel sleeve around the haft. The haft is round in section.

weapons.name: war-axe

firstPerson.why: the head comes from the icon; Patch kept the plain socket over the classic rounded socket and rings (#10575)

weapons.subject: A two-handed war axe: a long straight oiled wooden haft, and a steel head with two opposed crescent blades and a pointed spike at the top, fixed to a steel socket.
weapons.invent: The blades are flat and thin at their edges, thickening toward the socket. The socket is a short steel sleeve around the haft. The haft is round in section.

weapons.name: short-bow

firstPerson.why: its grey grip and steel rings differ from the icon's leather wrap, and the icon wins

weapons.subject: A short recurve bow: one continuous curved wooden stave, thicker at a leather-wrapped central grip and tapering to both tips, strung with one straight thin pale string.
weapons.invent: The stave is flattened in section and curves only in one plane. The string runs straight from tip to tip, and the bow is unstrung of any arrow; the arrow is its own model.

weapons.name: long-bow

firstPerson.why: its grey grip and steel rings differ from the icon's leather wrap, and the icon wins

weapons.subject: A tall plain longbow: one continuous long curved wooden stave, thicker at a leather-wrapped central grip and tapering to both tips, strung with one straight thin pale string.
weapons.invent: The stave is D-shaped in section and curves only in one plane. The string runs straight from tip to tip, and the bow is unstrung of any arrow; the arrow is its own model.

weapons.name: arrow
weapons.note: No paper-doll layer: its design is the accepted refreshed ground icon, authoring/gen-raw/items/texture-207-record-016.

firstPerson.why: the nocked arrow's thin shaft and green fletching agree with the ground icon

weapons.subject: One straight arrow: a barbed steel broadhead bound to a thin straight brown wooden shaft, with green and yellow feather fletching and a dark nock at the far end.
weapons.invent: The shaft is round in section. The broadhead is flat and thin at its edges. The feathers stand out from the shaft in three vanes spaced evenly round it.
